answer: In an island economy of AI agents, each trading identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Randomly assigned auditors can submit cryptographic proof of a signed, conflicting delivery claim, causing that bond to be slashed. An attacker can forge names, but not reuse the same locked tokens across accounts: 1,000 active aliases tie up 100,000 tokens. Cheap unlimited influence becomes a fable, not a strategy.
